chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from one of his companions (I think it was Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal or Ali ibn al-Hakam), from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who divorces his wife, when does she become irrevocably divorced from him? He said: When the blood emerges from the third menstruation, she controls herself. I said: So is it for her that she may marry in that state? He said: Yes, but she does not give herself over [to her husband] until she has purified from the blood.
ai.seo_question: When does a woman become irrevocably divorced after her husband divorces her three times?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise moment of irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in) by linking it to the emergence of blood from the third menstruation, a key indicator in Shia jurisprudence. While the woman gains autonomy to remarry at this point, the text specifies she must complete her purification (taharah) from that specific blood flow before the marriage contract can be finalized, reflecting the interplay between physical purity and legal status.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husay, from one of his companions, he thinks it was Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Hilal or Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who divorces his wife, when would she be irrevocably divorced from him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the blood emerges from the third menstruation, she would be in control of herself’. I said, ‘So, for her is that she can re-marry during that state?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but she cannot let her husband able over herself until she has purified from the blood’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from certain persons of his people, I think he is Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hilal or Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife and about when she becomes stranger to him. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is when blood of the third Hayd (menses) appears. She gets control of her own affairs.’ I then asked, ‘Can she marry in that condition?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, but she must not allow him to approach her before she is clean of blood of Hayd (menses).’
